topic_and_scope: Analysis of HIV-1 latent reservoir targeting strategies and their translational potential toward a cure, focusing on shock-and-kill, block-and-lock, broadly neutralizing antibodies, hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, cell-based immunotherapies, CRISPR/Cas9, and bispecific antibodies, and outlining key gaps and prioritized future directions.
main_themes: Persistence and heterogeneity of the HIV-1 latent reservoir and its resistance to current ART
Diverse reservoir-targeting modalities with potential synergy but significant translational hurdles
Safety, delivery, efficacy, and ethical considerations across cure strategies
main_findings: ART suppresses plasma viremia but fails to eradicate a long-lived latent reservoir, preventing a cure with current therapies.

Several reservoir-targeting strategies (CRISPR/Cas9, CAR T cells, bNAbs, LRAs, LEDGINs, etc.) show promise in preclinical and early clinical settings, but face major barriers including off-target effects, delivery challenges, limited reservoir reduction in vivo, and potential safety concerns.

key_gaps.description: Shock-and-kill strategies have not consistently reduced reservoir size in vivo, despite latency reversal, indicating insufficient clearance of reactivated cells or CNS-related safety risks.

CRISPR/Cas9-based approaches (proviral excision and host gene disruption) face off-target risks, limited in vivo delivery, potential immune responses, and scalability challenges that impede clinical translation.

future_directions.title: Develop and test combination shock-and-kill regimens with immune-augmentation and CNS safety monitoring
future_directions.rationale: The limited in vivo reservoir reduction with LRAs and concerns about neurotoxicity require integrating latency reversal with robust immune clearance strategies (e.g., bNAbs, CAR T cells, dendritic cell vaccines) and advanced CNS monitoring. Next steps include preclinical nonhuman primate studies incorporating comprehensive neuroinflammation imaging and CSF biomarkers, followed by early-phase human trials focusing on reservoir size, time to rebound after ART interruption, and safety endpoints in the CNS.

future_directions.title: Advance block-and-lock approaches with multiplex epigenetic and post-transcriptional silencing and evaluate durability
future_directions.rationale: Block-and-lock aims for permanent transcriptional silencing of proviruses; to achieve this, identify and validate combinations (e.g., LEDGINs, Tat inhibitors, mTOR modulators, splicing factors, RNA surveillance mechanisms) that sustain deep latency without reactivation. Concrete steps include testing in relevant animal models with ART withdrawal challenges, longitudinal safety assessments, and mechanistic studies of chromatin and transcript stability to determine durability and safety of permanent silencing.

future_directions.title: Develop long-acting, multi-epitope bNAb combinations and scalable delivery platforms
future_directions.rationale: bNAbs face limited half-life and resistance; engineering for extended activity and breadth across diverse HIV-1 strains is needed. Next steps involve creating long-acting formats (e.g., LS variants, gene-delivery approaches), evaluating combinations targeting non-overlapping epitopes in ART-suppressed individuals with diverse viral populations, optimizing dosing to prevent rebound during ATI, and monitoring anti-drug immune responses and tissue penetration.

future_directions.title: Refine multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 strategies with high-fidelity nucleases and safe in vivo delivery, plus autologous HSC approaches to address CXCR4/CCR5 tropism
future_directions.rationale: To overcome off-target concerns and delivery challenges, deploy multiplex gRNA strategies with high-fidelity nucleases (e.g., Cas variants, prime editing) and explore in vivo delivery modalities that maximize specificity. Simultaneously, pursue autologous stem cell approaches editing CCR5 and CXCR4 to broaden protection against HIV-1 tropisms. The plan includes testing in large-animal models, comprehensive off-target profiling, long-term safety monitoring, and progression toward carefully regulated clinical trials with robust ethical oversight.

future_directions.title: Optimize next-generation CAR T-cell strategies (e.g., duoCAR) with improved trafficking, persistence, and safety controls
future_directions.rationale: CAR T cells show strong in vivo activity but face persistence, trafficking to reservoirs, and safety issues like cytokine release syndrome. Future work should advance dual- or multi-epitope CAR designs, enhance homing to lymphoid and CNS reservoirs, incorporate safety switches, and evaluate combination with dendritic cell vaccines and checkpoint inhibitors. Preclinical models should emphasize durable control of viral rebound and safety in tissues that harbor latent virus.

future_directions.title: Advance bispecific antibodies with reduced immunogenicity and enhanced tissue penetration, tested in combination regimens
future_directions.rationale: Bispecific antibodies can increase avidity and recruit effector cells, but in vivo studies have shown challenges including anti-drug antibodies and limited efficacy in certain reservoirs. Develop bispecifics with optimized Fc domains and non-immunogenic formats, assess in SHIV/macaque models, monitor pharmacokinetics and tissue distribution, and test in combination with LRAs or CAR T cells to enhance clearance of infected cells while minimizing adverse immune reactions.

future_directions.title: Pioneer safer autologous stem cell–based approaches addressing CCR5 and CXCR4 to broaden patient eligibility and reduce transplant risks
future_directions.rationale: HSCT offers potential remission but carries high morbidity and fails against CXCR4-tropic variants. Future work should focus on autologous gene-edited HSCs with simultaneous CCR5 and CXCR4 resistance, refining conditioning regimens to reduce toxicity, and establishing ethical and equitable frameworks for patient selection. Early-phase trials should prioritize safety, immune reconstitution, reservoir impact, and quality of life in carefully selected populations.
